title: Symmetric-power nonvanishing and splitting off the unit after scalar extension
difficulty_reason: The new proof produces a universal pair of a vector and covector with contraction one by imposing the coevaluation relation in the symmetric algebra of M⊕M*. The maps α,β then split the unit. Establishing that the universal algebra is nonzero is the substantive step: projectivity of the free rank-one module yields a finite graded inverse to 1−δ̃ if the ideal is all of S; the diagonal recursion makes its coefficients powers of δ̃, forcing nilpotence. The coevaluation of each symmetric power identifies precisely when these powers vanish. The two implications and the construction are all present in the author text.

source_roles.source_label_caveats: The original PDF has S^n(M)≠0, I≠S and δ̃^n≠0. Indexed extraction loses inequality slashes. It prints δ rather than δ̃ in one equation before the immediately following correctly labelled recurrence. The computation is in S as indicated by the surrounding maps. No replacement proof or source edit.
source_roles.standard_local_support: The source cites 9.10.2 and 9.10.7 for the immediate symmetric-power/free-commutative algebra properties. The necessary restricted facts are that a functor preserves a given split retract, and that the symmetric algebra of a direct sum has the standard bigrading. The symmetric-power dual is obtained by dualizing the characteristic-zero symmetrizer idempotent, which also identifies the projected tensor-power coevaluation with the displayed δ̃^n. The projective/compact free unit A follows at the original setting from Hom_A(A,-)=Hom_C(1,-) on ind-objects. These are standard local checks, not proofs of the omitted exercises or of their later dimension applications.
